rows.conditions: Wood is a type of block that is generally obtained by cutting down trees using an axe or a chainsaw . Regular Wood can be harvested from Forest trees , vanity trees , Living Trees , and Underground Cabins in underground or cavern layers, as well as by using the Faecorn . Forest trees can be cultivated by placing Acorns on top of regular grass or Mowed grass above surface , and vanity trees can be cultivated by placing Sakura Sapling or Yellow Willow Sapling on top of any grass (but yields Ebonwood or Shadewood instead if placed on Corrupt or Crimson grass variants).

Some Wood types are found placed in other forms. For example, Underground Cabins generally use Wood corresponding to their biome (i.e. Rich Mahogany in the Jungle, Boreal in the Snow biome, regular Wood basically everywhere else). Living Trees and Living Mahogany Trees are made of Living Wood and Rich Mahogany, respectively.

There are 64 craftable tables and 5 noncraftable tables. Some tables can also be found in Underground Cabins , in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are in.

There are 60 types of Work Benches which can be crafted, and 5 types which must be picked up from areas such as the Dungeon . Some Work Benches can also be found in Underground Cabins , in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are found in.

Magic Mirrors can be found in Chests generated in the Underground and Cavern layers. Ice Mirrors can be found in Frozen Chests generated in the Ice biome . Newly created characters in Journey Mode (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) spawn with a Magic Mirror.

rows.notes: Vile Powder is able to convert blocks and walls, including the Crimson and the Hallowed ones, into their Corrupted form, such as converting Pearlstone into Ebonstone. If thrown at a Bunny , Penguin , or Goldfish , it will turn into its Corrupted variants: the Corrupt Bunny , Corrupt Penguin , and Corrupt Goldfish , respectively. It can be crafted from Vile Mushrooms or purchased from the Dryad for 1 SC each during a Blood Moon in a Corrupt world.

Vicious Powder is functionally identical to its counterpart, Vile Powder, to where it can convert blocks and walls, including the Corrupted and the Hallowed ones, into their Crimson form. If thrown at a Bunny, Penguin, or Goldfish, it will turn into its Crimson variants: the Vicious Bunny , Vicious Penguin , and Vicious Goldfish , respectively. It can be crafted from Vicious Mushrooms or purchased from the Dryad for 1 SC each during a Blood Moon in a Crimson world.

rows.conditions: Sand Blocks are soil blocks found in vast quantities in Desert biomes , at shore and bottom of Ocean biomes, and can be found as microbiomes in patches in the Underground layer. They are also shot as projectiles by Antlions . Sand can spread and be converted by the evil biomes and The Hallow (see below ).

Mud Blocks are a very common block type that comprises the majority of the Jungle , Underground Jungle , and Glowing Mushroom biome . It also generates in irregular patches in the Cavern layer. Mud Blocks may be covered by Jungle grass , Mushroom grass , Corrupt grass , or Crimson grass on any side, which can be planted with Jungle Grass Seeds , Mushroom Grass Seeds , Corrupt Seeds , and Crimson Seeds . Only Jungle grass and Mushroom grass are incapable of growing on Dirt Blocks .

rows.conditions: Silt Blocks are a type of soil blocks that generates in the Underground and Cavern layers, appearing more frequently at lower depths. Silt is affected by gravity and will deal damage to any player or enemy it falls on. Unlike Sand Blocks , silt can stop the Hallow , the Crimson , and the Corruption from spreading. Silt looks similar to Ash Blocks , but is a lighter color.

rows.conditions: The Holy Arrow is a Hardmode arrow . Upon contact with enemies or blocks , two Hallow Star projectiles will fall from the sky to the impact location. The stars deal 1/3 (33.33%) of the combined damage of the arrow and weapon, and do not pierce.

rows.notes: The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 GC . When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End) , which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 GC after defeating the Moon Lord .

The Living Mahogany Wand places Living Mahogany blocks at the cost of one Rich Mahogany each. The blocks placed are the same as those found in Living Mahogany Trees . Recorded while equipped
rows.notes: Recorded Music Box variant from a blank Music Box

The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 GC . When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End) , which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 GC after defeating the Moon Lord .

When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End) , which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 GC after defeating the Moon Lord .

Recorded while equipped
rows.notes: Recorded Music Box variant from a blank Music Box

The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 GC . When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End) , which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 GC after defeating the Moon Lord .

rows.notes: Recorded Music Box variant from a blank Music Box

The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 GC . When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End) , which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 GC after defeating the Moon Lord .

rows.notes: Vile Powder is able to convert blocks and walls, including the Crimson and the Hallowed ones, into their Corrupted form, such as converting Pearlstone into Ebonstone. If thrown at a Bunny , Penguin , or Goldfish , it will turn into its Corrupted variants: the Corrupt Bunny , Corrupt Penguin , and Corrupt Goldfish , respectively. It can be crafted from Vile Mushrooms or purchased from the Dryad for 1 SC each during a Blood Moon in a Corrupt world.

Vicious Powder is functionally identical to its counterpart, Vile Powder, to where it can convert blocks and walls, including the Corrupted and the Hallowed ones, into their Crimson form. If thrown at a Bunny, Penguin, or Goldfish, it will turn into its Crimson variants: the Vicious Bunny , Vicious Penguin , and Vicious Goldfish , respectively. It can be crafted from Vicious Mushrooms or purchased from the Dryad for 1 SC each during a Blood Moon in a Crimson world.

The Weather Radio can be received as a 1/34 (2.94%) [ 1 ] chance reward for completing a fishing quest for the Angler NPC , depending on the number of completed quests and other factors (see Angler § Quest rewards for details) . The Angler will not give the player a Weather Radio as a reward if they already have one in their inventory or in any of their portable storage items or loadouts . However, if the player has all of the Angler's fishing and informational accessories [ 2 ] (or their upgrades like the Angler Tackle Bag and Fish Finder ) in their inventories, this rule will be ignored. rows.conditions: Recorded while equipped
rows.notes: Recorded Music Box variant from a blank Music Box

The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 GC . When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End) , which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 GC after defeating the Moon Lord .

rows.notes: Planter Boxes are flat-surface items of furniture purchased from the Dryad for 1 SC each in which herb or flower seeds can be planted. If left empty, wild grass plants will randomly grow out of them, provided the box is placed on the surface or in Space . [ 1 ] The plant in a Planter Box cannot be cut in the regular manner, e.g. via nearby swinging tools. Instead, it needs to be removed with a pickaxe or drill , or the Staff of Regrowth or Axe of Regrowth .

The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 GC . When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End) , which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 GC after defeating the Moon Lord .

rows.conditions: Sandstone Blocks are blocks found naturally placed in the Underground Desert biome . Like Sand and Hardened Sand , they are corruptable blocks in Hardmode, and have Corruption , Crimson , and Hallowed counterparts: Ebonsandstone , Crimsandstone , and Pearlsandstone respectively.

The Sandstone Wall , Ebonsandstone Wall , Crimsandstone Wall , and Pearlsandstone Wall are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Underground Desert , considered unsafe . Underground Deserts generate by default the normal Sandstone Sand Wall which may be converted into the respective variant if exposed to the Corruption , Crimson , or Hallow . Converted Sandstone Walls may further spread conversion to other walls; see Biome spread for more information. Unsafe Sandstone Walls do not drop as items when destroyed, and can only be obtained via crafting. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player.

rows.conditions: Treasure Bags are consumable grab bag -like items obtained in Expert Mode and Master Mode as a reward for defeating bosses . The contents and appearance of Treasure Bags depend on the boss it comes from, and are opened by using either ⚷ Open / Activate while inside the inventory , or ⚒ Use / Attack when selected in the hotbar . They emit light and have a special effect around them when dropped, making them easier to spot. In multiplayer , each player that deals damage to the boss receives one Treasure Bag upon defeating it. Treasure Bags are client-side and will despawn upon exiting the world. See Notes for details.

The Hardened Sand Wall , Hardened Ebonsand Wall , Hardened Crimsand Wall , and Hardened Pearlsand Wall are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Underground Desert , considered unsafe . Underground Deserts generate by default the normal Hardened Sand Wall which may be converted into the respective variant if exposed to the Corruption , Crimson , or Hallow . Converted Hardened Sand Walls may further spread conversion; see Biome spread for more information. Unsafe Hardened Sand Walls do not drop as items when destroyed, and can only be obtained via crafting. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player.

The Bone Wand places Bone Blocks at the cost of one Bone per block. The block can be mined back as Bone. The Bone Wand has a 1/250 (0.4%) chance to drop from Angry Bones , Dark Casters , Librarian Skeletons and Cursed Skulls , which spawn in the Dungeon .

The Living Mahogany Wand places Living Mahogany blocks at the cost of one Rich Mahogany each. The blocks placed are the same as those found in Living Mahogany Trees . The Living Mahogany Wand has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being found alongside the Rich Mahogany Leaf Wand in Ivy Chests found within Living Mahogany Trees and Jungle Shrines in the Underground Jungle biome , and can also be obtained by shaking Jungle trees .

The Rich Mahogany Leaf Wand places Mahogany Leaf Blocks at the cost of one Rich Mahogany each. The blocks placed are the same as found in Living Mahogany Trees and have the same properties. The Rich Mahogany Leaf Wand has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being found alongside the Living Mahogany Wand in Ivy Chests found within Living Mahogany Trees and Jungle Shrines in the Underground Jungle biome , and can also be obtained by shaking Jungle trees .

The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 GC . When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End) , which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 GC after defeating the Moon Lord .

Trophies are decorative furniture items which usually have a 1/10 (10%) chance to be dropped from most bosses . While they can be considered the "boss version of banners ", they are purely cosmetic and do not provide any bonuses. Some trophies can only be rewarded by the Angler for completing fishing quests . In total, there are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 33 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 24 trophies.

Statues are furniture items. While some are purely decorative, others have a functional effect when activated via Wire —depending on the statue, it may spawn enemies , drop items , or teleport an NPC to the statue's location. Most statues can be found already placed in any area underground (most frequently in the Dungeon , Underground Cabins , and Cavern level), though Angel Statues also appear in Chests . Like all furniture, a pickaxe , a drill , or explosives are used to collect them.

rows.notes: Recorded Music Box variant from a blank Music Box

The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 GC . When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End) , which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 GC after defeating the Moon Lord .

Treasure Bags are consumable grab bag -like items obtained in Expert Mode and Master Mode as a reward for defeating bosses . The contents and appearance of Treasure Bags depend on the boss it comes from, and are opened by using either ⚷ Open / Activate while inside the inventory , or ⚒ Use / Attack when selected in the hotbar . They emit light and have a special effect around them when dropped, making them easier to spot. In multiplayer , each player that deals damage to the boss receives one Treasure Bag upon defeating it. Treasure Bags are client-side and will despawn upon exiting the world. See Notes for details.

The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 GC . When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End) , which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 GC after defeating the Moon Lord .

The Dead Man's Chest is a naturally-generated Chest rigged with a large variety of traps in order to kill the player upon opening it. This setup usually includes 3–5 Boulder traps , 2–6 Dart Traps , and 0–3 Explosives , with a possibility of 1–2 Geysers if generated at depths in which lava can spawn naturally. The Boulder traps are set up above the chest, the Dart Traps are set up horizontally, and the Explosives are hidden underneath.

Decorative statues have no function and only serve as decoration. They are generally found placed underground . The three Lihzahrd statues are only found in the Jungle Temple , and are the only statues that do not appear to be made of stone. The Armor Statue can also be crafted with 50 at a Work Bench .

There are 5 types of regular moss: Green Moss, Brown Moss, Red Moss, Blue Moss, and Purple Moss. One of each regular moss can be found throughout each third of a given map (three variants per world). They can be found either randomly on cave surfaces or in moss chambers with a matching Mossy Wall.

Glowing mosses are special variants of moss that glow in vibrant colors. These include the Lava Moss, Krypton Moss, Xenon Moss, Argon Moss, Neon Moss, and Helium Moss. Lava Moss can be found in patches around the lava layer of the Caverns . Krypton, Xenon, Argon, and Neon Moss grow in glowing moss biomes and in much larger areas than other mosses, and only one type among these can be found in each world. Up to two ( small world ) / three ( medium world ) / four ( large world ) glowing moss biomes will be generated in the Cavern layer, mostly above the lava layers, but not near the horizontal center of the world. Helium Moss does not spawn naturally and can instead be obtained by throwing any other glowing moss into Shimmer .

rows.notes: The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 GC . When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End) , which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 GC after defeating the Moon Lord .

Advanced Combat Techniques is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the defense of Town NPCs by 8, their attack damage by 25%, their attack speed by 20%, and their health by 250. Advanced Combat Techniques can only be obtained by fishing during a Blood Moon . It can only be used once per world, and others cannot be fished up once one has already been used. However, multiple copies can be obtained until the first is used. The chance of fishing it up when conditions are met is 1/360 (0.28%) with 50 Fishing Power and 1/180 (0.56%) with 100 Fishing Power (assuming neither Crate Potion nor Chum Caster is used and that the body of water is not too small).

rows.conditions: Treasure Bags are consumable grab bag -like items obtained in Expert Mode and Master Mode as a reward for defeating bosses . The contents and appearance of Treasure Bags depend on the boss it comes from, and are opened by using either ⚷ Open / Activate while inside the inventory , or ⚒ Use / Attack when selected in the hotbar . They emit light and have a special effect around them when dropped, making them easier to spot. In multiplayer , each player that deals damage to the boss receives one Treasure Bag upon defeating it. Treasure Bags are client-side and will despawn upon exiting the world. See Notes for details.

Trophies are decorative furniture items which usually have a 1/10 (10%) chance to be dropped from most bosses . While they can be considered the "boss version of banners ", they are purely cosmetic and do not provide any bonuses. Some trophies can only be rewarded by the Angler for completing fishing quests . In total, there are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 33 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 24 trophies.
Fishing trophies are rewarded randomly by the Angler NPC for completing quests.

The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 GC . When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End) , which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 GC after defeating the Moon Lord .

Relics are furniture items dropped by bosses and mini-bosses in Master Mode . They are golden depictions of their respective boss that hover above a pedestal, have a golden particle effect, and emit light when placed close to a light source .

rows.conditions: Treasure Bags are consumable grab bag -like items obtained in Expert Mode and Master Mode as a reward for defeating bosses . The contents and appearance of Treasure Bags depend on the boss it comes from, and are opened by using either ⚷ Open / Activate while inside the inventory , or ⚒ Use / Attack when selected in the hotbar . They emit light and have a special effect around them when dropped, making them easier to spot. In multiplayer , each player that deals damage to the boss receives one Treasure Bag upon defeating it. Treasure Bags are client-side and will despawn upon exiting the world. See Notes for details.

There are 5 types of regular moss: Green Moss, Brown Moss, Red Moss, Blue Moss, and Purple Moss. One of each regular moss can be found throughout each third of a given map (three variants per world). They can be found either randomly on cave surfaces or in moss chambers with a matching Mossy Wall.

Glowing mosses are special variants of moss that glow in vibrant colors. These include the Lava Moss, Krypton Moss, Xenon Moss, Argon Moss, Neon Moss, and Helium Moss. Lava Moss can be found in patches around the lava layer of the Caverns . Krypton, Xenon, Argon, and Neon Moss grow in glowing moss biomes and in much larger areas than other mosses, and only one type among these can be found in each world. Up to two ( small world ) / three ( medium world ) / four ( large world ) glowing moss biomes will be generated in the Cavern layer, mostly above the lava layers, but not near the horizontal center of the world. Helium Moss does not spawn naturally and can instead be obtained by throwing any other glowing moss into Shimmer .

rows.notes: Recorded Music Box variant from a blank Music Box

The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 GC . When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End) , which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 GC after defeating the Moon Lord .

rows.conditions: The Sandstone Wall , Ebonsandstone Wall , Crimsandstone Wall , and Pearlsandstone Wall are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Underground Desert , considered unsafe . Underground Deserts generate by default the normal Sandstone Sand Wall which may be converted into the respective variant if exposed to the Corruption , Crimson , or Hallow . Converted Sandstone Walls may further spread conversion to other walls; see Biome spread for more information. Unsafe Sandstone Walls do not drop as items when destroyed, and can only be obtained via crafting. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player.

Demon Altars and Crimson Altars are naturally-occurring crafting stations found mainly in and around chasms in The Corruption or Crimson , and less frequently underground . They are used to craft pre-Hardmode boss -summoning items and the Night's Edge as well as the Void Bag and Vault . Placed altars emit some light, making them easy to spot. They cannot be freed, picked up, or crafted. A Demon or Crimson Altar item will drop from the Eye of Cthulhu if no altars are present in the world.

Recorded while equipped
rows.notes: Recorded Music Box variant from a blank Music Box

The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 GC . When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End) , which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 GC after defeating the Moon Lord .

rows.conditions: The Dirt Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in most caves and under overhangs on the surface , considered unsafe . It does not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained via crafting. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player.

rows.conditions: Enemy banners are functional furniture items that can be placed on the underside of blocks and platforms . They are obtained by killing most enemies and a few critters .
Shimmer transmutation
rows.notes: Dull Team Block variant from Red Team Block

Team Blocks are decorative blocks purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 1 SC each. Team Blocks are available in six different colors, each representing one of the six team colors selectable in the player's inventory , including white for the neutral team. They can be transmuted into their respective "dull" variant via Shimmer .

Demon Altars and Crimson Altars are naturally-occurring crafting stations found mainly in and around chasms in The Corruption or Crimson , and less frequently underground . They are used to craft pre-Hardmode boss -summoning items and the Night's Edge as well as the Void Bag and Vault . Placed altars emit some light, making them easy to spot. They cannot be freed, picked up, or crafted. A Demon or Crimson Altar item will drop from the Eye of Cthulhu if no altars are present in the world.

rows.notes: Recorded Music Box variant from a blank Music Box

The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 GC . When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End) , which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 GC after defeating the Moon Lord .
